brief:
Palestinian and Levantine artists are addressing their regions' traumatic histories through works including massacre locations painted onto basalt slabs and photocollages depicting bulldozed airports, The Guardian reported. The exhibition, presented at IMMA in Dublin, features contributions from artists across the Levant responding to displacement, destruction, and violence through visual testimony.

Syrian artist Simone Fattal began this practice in 2006, inscribing massacre sites onto stone as a method of commemoration. The works collectively invoke a landscape where, as one artist's statement suggests, violence pervades even natural elements—"in our lands the rain is made of bullets."
dek: IMMA, Dublin From massacre locations painted on to basalt slabs to photocollages of bulldozed airports, artists from across the Levant address their traumatic history In 2006, Simone Fattal painted on to basalt slabs the names of places indelibly associated…
title: Palestinian artists confront trauma through massacre imagery and sculptural memory
